cards.headline: Night-owl volume bidder who lives in the cap-free pool and inflates prices as a serial underbidder, but rarely closes the marquee — a nuisance and price-pusher, not a marquee rival to Keith.
cards.bid_rhythm: Hard nocturnal. SF-era peak_hours_et = 23, 22, 13, and the hour_hist bears it out: 43 bids land in the 23:00 ET hour and 32 in the 22:00 hour — by far the heaviest two buckets, dwarfing every daytime hour. There is a secondary ~13:00 ET (1pm) lunch pulse (13 bids). High raw volume — 233 bids for only 60 wins (~3.9 bids per win) spread broadly — but the clicking concentrates into the 10pm–midnight ET window. Expect him most live when other owners are asleep.
cards.snipe_threat: Real and his standout trait. post_win_pounce_share = 0.65 — after ~two-thirds of his wins he is bidding on another lot within 8h — and post_win_avg_followups = 2.47, so each win tends to spawn ~2-3 more bids. Winning a lot does not pull him out of the room; it accelerates him into a chain of further pickups in the same late-night session. Practical read: if Keith wins a lot, Ryan won't retaliate on that lot, but he'll immediately swing at whatever else is still open.
cards.lurk_threat: High-frequency underbidder, low conversion. runner_up_n = 43 in the SF era (51 over L5) — his bridesmaid count nearly matches his 60 wins, so he is constantly the guy who pushes the winner up and then loses. lurk_win_n = 0: sitting as the underbidder essentially never converts to a win for him. late_bid_share is only moderate (under8h 0.348, under6h 0.326, under2h 0.287) — about a third of his action is inside the final 8h, but he is not a true last-second sniper; most overtakes land 24–90h out (Mike Evans pushed to $36k bumping 0010 at 45.3h, Hopkins to $26k at 43.2h). overtake_rate 0.245, late_overtake_n only 7. Net: he inflates prices far more than he steals lots.
cards.spend_signature: Bargain-bin specialist. zone_mix = capfree 0.733 / low 0.117 / mid 0.083 / marquee 0.067 — far more cap-free-skewed than the league (league capfree 0.611, marquee 0.126), i.e. he plays marquee about half as often as the field. Only 4 marquee_wins and a max_win_k of just $38k (Derek Carr, 2022) — well under the league's top SF wins ($94k Henry, $66k Brady). SF positional spend tilts WR $65k / QB $64k / RB $64k, then TE $35k and LB $23k — note the meaningful LB line for an offense-heavy field. He spreads $286k across 60 wins (~$4.8k avg, right at the league median win of $4k), confirming a wide-and-shallow, value-hunting style rather than star-hunting.
cards.vs_0008: Medium threat to Keith — disruptive on the margins, not at the top. (1) PRICE-PUSHER, not a thief: with runner_up_n 43 and lurk_win_n 0, Ryan's main effect on Keith is bidding Keith's targets up and then bowing out; Keith can let Ryan run the early price and still expect to win contested lots, since Ryan rarely converts. (2) He has already poked Keith 7 times in the SF era (overtakes vs victim_fid 0008): Trubisky $5k, Russell Gage $5k, Mike Evans $5k, Spillane $2k, Flacco $2k, Rousseau $2k, Aubrey $2k — every single one cheap/cap-free, never a marquee fight. So the clash zone is the $2–5k scrap pool, not Keith's big swings. (3) TIMING: Keith should place real bids in the 10pm–midnight ET window only if he intends to win, because that's Ryan's active hour and he'll volume-bid filler up; conversely, lots Keith genuinely wants are safer parked when Ryan is offline (early/mid afternoon outside the 1pm pulse). (4) POUNCE GUARD: after Keith wins anything, expect Ryan to immediately work other open lots (pounce 0.65, ~2.5 followups) — so if Keith and Ryan share a watchlist of cheap LBs/QBs, get the must-haves locked early rather than leaving them in the late pool where Ryan is chaining. Bottom line: don't overpay to out-muscle him on marquee (he won't be there), but don't leave cheap targets exposed in his 22:00–23:00 ET prime time.
key_examples: 2022: Won Derek Carr (QB) for $38k — his single largest SF-era win and one of only 4 marquee_wins; got there by overtaking 0002 up the ladder, illustrating he'll commit at QB but tops out ~$38k vs the league's $66k QB ceiling.

2022: Pushed Mike Evans (WR) to $36k as the underbidder against 0010 and LOST, then again chased Evans to $21k in 2024 (vs 0012) and lost — a textbook runner_up_n=43 pattern of inflating a star's price without closing.

SF-era overtakes directly against Keith (0008) are all cap-free scraps: Mitch Trubisky $5k (2022), Russell Gage $5k (2022), Mike Evans $5k (2024), Robert Spillane LB $2k, Joe Flacco $2k, Greg Rousseau DE $2k, Brandon Aubrey PK $2k (all 2024-25) — the Keith collision zone is the $2–5k bin, never the marquee.

Pounce in action: in 2022 he won Bobby Wagner (LB, $9k) and Robert Woods (WR, $13k) and Derek Carr ($38k) within the same active stretch — consistent with post_win_pounce_share 0.65 / 2.47 followups, where one win triggers a chain of further late-night bids.

cards.headline: A cap-free grinder who mostly nibbles, but will lurch awake to snipe a marquee WR/RB right at the 24h lock — and twice has ripped a built-up lot straight out of Keith's hands.
cards.bid_rhythm: Early-morning bidder: SF peak_hours_et are 8, 9, 0 (his hour_hist spikes at hr8=22 and hr9=19, plus an overnight/midnight cluster of 18 at hr0). Activity is spread across the clock rather than one window, but the live danger sits in the morning ET hours and at midnight, not the evening. His bids run LATE in the lock cycle: SF late_bid_share is under8h 0.369, under6h 0.352, under2h 0.336 — over a third of his bids land with under 2h on the clock, so he is a back-half-of-the-window operator who lets a lot ripen and pounces near close.
cards.snipe_threat: Real post-win activity: SF post_win_pounce_share is 0.423 with post_win_avg_followups 1.25 (L5 nearly identical: 0.417 / 1.28). So after roughly 4 of every 10 wins he immediately bids on at least one more lot within 8h, averaging ~1.25 follow-ups. He is not a relentless serial sniper, but a win does NOT take him out of the room — expect one or two opportunistic follow-on bids while Keith is still mid-fight on the next player.
cards.lurk_threat: Genuine lurk/late-overtake threat. SF runner_up_n=18 (L5=23) — he is frequently the underbidder/bridesmaid who pushes the winner up and loses, so he is constantly applying price pressure even when he walks away empty. His SF overtake_rate is 0.133 with late_overtake_n=1 (L5 late_overtake_n=3): he rarely waits til the final 2h to do the overtaking, but he DOES swoop. Documented: 2024 Kamara — Keith (0008) built the lot to 26k, then at the 24h mark 0002 came over the top at 27k (is_overtake=1, victim_fid=0008, seq17) and won at 27k. He sits as the second-highest bidder more than almost anything else he does.
cards.spend_signature: Overwhelmingly a cap-free dabbler: SF zone_mix is capfree 0.865 / low 0.058 / mid 0.038 / marquee 0.038 — 86.5% of his action is the 2-4K bargain bin (vs league capfree 0.611). But he carries a marquee streak: SF marquee_wins=2, max_win_k=32.0 (DeAndre Hopkins 2022), and his all-time book includes Antonio Brown at 79k (2019) and Keenan Allen at 60k (2021), so he can detonate. Position appetite tilts pass-catcher/back: SF pos_spend_k WR 55k, RB 42k, QB 28k — exactly Keith's wheelhouse. 52 SF wins on 180 bids, total 172k.
cards.vs_0008: He directly collides with Keith on the positions Keith spends on (WR 55k / RB 42k SF) and has TWICE won a lot that 0008 was actively building. 2022 Hopkins: Keith opened at 1k, 0002 overtook him at 5k (vic=0008) and then late-laddered 27→28→32k to win at 32k. 2024 Kamara: Keith pushed it to 26k, 0002 sniped at 27k over the top of 0008 at the 24h lock and won. Across his book he forced/pushed 0008 on 17 separate bids (Edelman 30k 2014, Kamara 27k, Hopkins). And in 2021 he won Keenan Allen at 60k with 0008 as the runner_up — Keith was the bridesmaid that time. Handling: do NOT let Whitman set the closing price on a WR/RB Keith truly wants — his danger is concentrated in the morning ET hours (8-9) and the final-2h window (33.6% of bids under 2h), so Keith should place his decisive ladder bid AFTER Whitman's typical morning/late surge or be prepared to jump him at the lock rather than nominate-and-coast. Because 86.5% of his bids are cap-free junk, treat his early 2-4k pokes as noise; the tell that he is serious is a mid-window jump on a marquee WR/RB — that's when to either commit hard early or let him have it, never leave a half-built marquee lot exposed at the 24h mark.
key_examples: 2022 DeAndre Hopkins (WR): Keith (0008) opened at 1k; 0002 overtook 0008 at 5k (seq3, vic=0008), then late-laddered 27→28→32k inside the final 24h to WIN at 32k — his SF max_win and a marquee_win, taken off a Keith-opened lot.

2024 Alvin Kamara (RB): Keith built the price to 26k (seq16); at the 24h lock 0002 came over the top at 27k (seq17, is_overtake=1, victim_fid=0008) and won at 27k — a textbook late-overtake snipe on a Keith-built RB.

2021 Keenan Allen (WR): 0002 WON at 60k with runner_up_fid=0008 — Keith was the underbidder who pushed Whitman to his second-highest career price; proof Whitman will chase a marquee WR all the way up against Keith.
2019 Antonio Brown (WR): all-time max win at 79k — evidence that despite an 86.5% cap-free SF profile, Whitman is capable of a true marquee detonation when motivated.

cards.headline: A relentless cap-free grinder who lurks late, overtakes often, and has personally jacked up Keith's price on a marquee RB.
cards.bid_rhythm: Daytime-active and spread across the clock. SF peak ET hours are 12, 14, 16 (a midday-into-afternoon window), with secondary spikes at hours 9, 17, and 20. The L5 hour_hist also lights up hour 0 (20 bids) and hour 20 (19), so he is reachable from noon to late night, not a single tight window. Critically he bids LATE: 52.2% of SF bids land under 8h to close, 50.0% under 6h, and 47.1% under 2h — nearly half his action is in the final two hours before the 24h lock.
cards.snipe_threat: Real and consistent. post_win_pounce_share is 0.522 in SF (0.518 over L5) with post_win_avg_followups of 1.15 — after winning a lot he bids on another within 8h more than half the time. He does not bank a win and go quiet; expect him to immediately roll momentum into a second target, so his wins should be treated as a signal to recheck your own watchlist, not relief.
cards.lurk_threat: High. He is the prototype underbidder/bridesmaid: runner_up_n is 17 in SF (25 over L5) — he loses a lot of bid wars, but only after pushing the winner's price up. overtake_rate 0.183 with late_overtake_n 8 (11 over L5) means he actively re-bids in the closing hours: of 38 SF overtakes, multiple land inside the final ~36h (e.g. 2025 Etienne at $16 t_close 24.02h over 0004; 2024 Henry at $34 t_close 24.04h over 0002; 2024 Singletary at $21 t_close 24.03h over 0001). lurk_win_n is 0, so he rarely steals the lot outright — his weapon is the late tax he applies on the way to losing.
cards.spend_signature: Volume-over-stars value hunter. SF zone_mix is 80.6% cap-free (2-4K), 7.5% low, just 1.5% mid, and 10.4% marquee — far more cap-free-skewed than the league (61.1% cap-free / 12.6% marquee). 67 SF wins on 208 bids for $311K total. Position spend (SF) leans RB $94K, QB $70K, WR $67K, TE $33K, with a real IDP appetite (LB $15K, S $9K). marquee_wins 7, max_win_k $37K (Kirk Cousins QB, 2022). Other marquee wins: Derrick Henry RB $34K (2024), Chris Godwin WR $27K (2023), David Njoku TE $27K (2025), Devin Singletary RB $21K (2024), D.J. Moore WR $21K (2025), Sam Darnold QB $18K (2025). He will splurge a few times a summer but lives in the cap-free bargain bin.
cards.vs_0008: Gerardi is a direct, repeat antagonist on Keith's lots. In the SF era he has overtaken 0008 four times: Kamara $5K (2024), Travis Kelce $12K (2025), Deebo Samuel $7K t_close 24.02h (2025), and most importantly Chuba Hubbard $34K (2025). The Hubbard war is the tell — Keith opened the bidding ($15→$20), Gerardi climbed in at $23→$24→$26→$28 then overtook Keith directly at $34 (seq11), forcing Keith to grind up to $36→$37 to finally win at $37 (a $17 premium over Keith's $20 opener that Gerardi personally manufactured). Tactic vs 0008: (1) Because he is a cap-free grinder, do NOT engage him in the 2-4K bin — he will outlast you on volume and it is wasted ammo; concede the scraps. (2) On YOUR marquee RB/WR/TE targets, expect him to appear late (sub-2h) and as an overtaker, so do not show your ceiling early — his 47.1% sub-2h share means a comfortable lead at hour 12 is not safe at hour 23. Place your true max in the final window so he cannot ratchet you up incrementally like he did on Hubbard. (3) Treat any Gerardi win as a snipe warning (52.2% pounce) and re-cover your other open lots immediately. (4) His IDP/TE spend (Njoku $27K, LB $15K) overlaps Keith's needs — pre-empt those at a price above his marquee comfort to avoid a bidding ladder.
key_examples: 2025 Chuba Hubbard RB: Gerardi (0003) climbed $23→$28 then overtook Keith (0008) at $34 with 35h left (seq11); Keith was forced up to $37 to win — Gerardi added roughly $17 to Keith's bill on a lot he did not even win.
2022 Kirk Cousins QB $37K — his max win and a marquee QB grab, overtaking 0010 from $17; shows he will go to the top of the QB market when motivated.
2024 Derrick Henry RB $34K, won at hour 19 with t_close 24.04h after overtaking 0002 — a late-window marquee overtake that became a win.
2025 Deebo Samuel WR: Gerardi overtook Keith (0008) at $7K with just 24.02h to close — a textbook late re-bid directly on a Keith lot.

cards.headline: A heavy-spending RB/QB whale who dawn-patrols the board, pounces on 67% of his wins, and has already pushed Keith to a $94K record and out-dueled him for Kelce.
cards.bid_rhythm: Hard morning bidder: SF-era peak_hours_et are 6, 7, 12 ET, with the hour_hist stacking 42 bids at 6am and 38 at 7am ET (vs only a few in the 17:00-21:00 evening window). He fires when most owners are asleep, then a midday top-up at noon (30 bids in the 12:00 bucket). Not primarily a last-second sniper — late_bid_share is moderate (under8h 0.244, under6h 0.228, under2h 0.191), so ~1 in 5 of his bids land in the final 2 hours but the bulk are placed early and often (300 SF-era bids for only 61 wins).
cards.snipe_threat: Elite pouncer — this is his most dangerous trait. SF-era post_win_pounce_share is 0.672 (he bids on another lot within 8h of two-thirds of his wins) with post_win_avg_followups 2.64. Verified in the DB: the minute after winning McCaffrey at 07:47:30 (2025) he was bidding Aiyuk at 07:48:44 and Njoku ($16K) at 07:49:26, then chased Etienne, Kelce, and Rodgers across the same day. Winning one lot does NOT take him off the board; it accelerates him.
cards.lurk_threat: Real bridesmaid/late-overtake threat. runner_up_n is 24 (SF) — he is frequently the underbidder who drives the price up and loses. late_overtake_n is 7 with overtake_rate 0.27, and he will jump late to steal: on his own McCaffrey 2025 win he sat at $45K then leaped to $56K at 20:44 ET to lock it. His losses cluster on premium RB/QB: he pushed Ekeler to $57K (lost to 0009, 2022), Prescott to $50K (lost to 0002, 2024), and Tyreek Hill to $61K (lost to 0007, 2024) — meaning his presence inflates every marquee skill-position lot whether or not he wins it.
cards.spend_signature: Top-of-market money concentrated on RB and QB. SF-era total_k 430 across 61 wins; pos_spend_k is RB 125 / QB 106 / WR 71 / TE 47 — RB+QB = 54% of spend. zone_mix is capfree 0.672 / low 0.131 / mid 0.082 / marquee 0.115, and he has 7 marquee_wins (18K+) in the SF era: McCaffrey $56K, Prescott $45K, Mayfield $31K, Davante Adams $30K, Keenan Allen $28K, Goedert $22K, Kelce $21K. max_win_k is 56.0 (McCaffrey 2025). He is comfortable spending into the p90+ of every position (league RB p90 is 27K, QB p90 38K — he routinely clears both).
cards.vs_0008: Direct, proven antagonist to Keith. In 2023 0004 was the runner-up who forced Keith (0008) to the league-record $94K for Derrick Henry — his own top bid hit $65K and his $54K/$52K bids list 0008 as the party he was forcing. That cost Keith ~$40K of cap he wouldn't have spent unopposed. In 2025 0004 BEAT Keith head-to-head for Travis Kelce ($21K, with Keith as the forced underbidder at the $9-10K rungs). Tactics for Keith: (1) Expect him on every premium RB/QB Keith nominates — bake a 0004 premium into the budget or nominate Keith's RB/QB targets at off-hours he's less active. (2) Beat his dawn patrol — get a firm lead in before the 6-7am ET window or be ready to defend at noon; do not assume a quiet overnight lot is safe. (3) Respect the late jump — he overtook from $45K to $56K on his own McCaffrey win, so a comfortable evening lead on a marquee player is not safe from him near close. (4) Use him as a price-setter against others: he will inflate a lot then lose (runner_up_n 24), so if Keith doesn't want the player, let 0004 bid the field up and bleed a rival's cap.
key_examples: Derrick Henry 2023 RB: 0004 was the underbidder who pushed Keith (0008) to the league-record $94K, topping out at his own $65K bid and forcing 0008 at the $54K/$52K rungs — directly cost Keith cap.

Christian McCaffrey 2025 RB ($56K, his max win): sat at $45K then late-overtook to $56K at 20:44 ET, and one minute after the 07:47 lock was already bidding Aiyuk (07:48) and Njoku $16K (07:49) — pounce in action.
Travis Kelce 2025 TE ($21K win): out-dueled Keith (0008) head-to-head, with Keith left as the forced underbidder at the $9-10K rungs.

Marquee losses where he inflated the price and bowed out: Ekeler $57K (to 0009, 2022), Prescott $50K (to 0002, 2024), Tyreek Hill $61K (to 0007, 2024) — runner_up_n 24 confirms he is a serial price-driver.

cards.headline: A morning-shift RB/QB bully who has out-muscled Keith 11-2 in head-to-head lots and pounces on a second target after almost every win.
cards.bid_rhythm: Daytime/early aggressor, NOT a midnight sniper. SF-era peak ET hours are 5, 12, 8 (hour_hist: 27 bids at 5am, 24 at noon, 18 at 8am ET; next cluster is 0:00 with 12). The headline late_bid_share (under8h 0.306 / under6h 0.290 / under2h 0.258) is misleading — strip the auto-close rows and only 2 of his 174 SF bids were genuinely placed with <8h left (Conner $38k at 0.03h, Hines $8k at 4.5h). His real M.O. is to seize the lead DAYS early: of 53 SF overtakes, nearly all land at t_to_close of 24-100h, not the final hours. Focused morning/lunch windows, not a wide spread.
cards.snipe_threat: Heavy pouncer — his most dangerous trait for board flow. post_win_pounce_share 0.705 (SF) / 0.711 (L5): after ~7 of every 10 wins he's bidding on another lot within 8h, averaging 1.39 follow-ups (SF) / 1.89 (L5). He doesn't bank a win and rest — landing a player triggers him to immediately go shopping again. Expect him to win a target and then appear on the very next RB/QB you nominate.
cards.lurk_threat: Active overtaker, not a passive lurker (lurk_win_n=0 — he never sits quiet as the underbidder to steal at the buzzer). overtake_rate 0.305 across 53 SF overtakes, but late_overtake_n is only 3 — his overtakes are early, not last-second. He is a frequent bridesmaid though: runner_up_n=8 (SF) / 14 (L5), and a broader cut shows him pushing the eventual winner up on 16 SF lots (Fournette to $39k after he hit $35k; Conner to $38k matching his own $38k; Godwin to $27k). He inflates prices even when he loses.
cards.spend_signature: RB-first, QB-second. SF pos_spend: RB $122k, QB $75k, WR $49k, then IDP (LB $21k, S $20k, DE $13k); $319k total over 61 wins. Mostly value-shopping — zone_mix is 78.7% cap-free (2-4K), only ~8% each mid and marquee — but he WILL spike: marquee_wins=5, max_win $41k (Mixon 2023). Big wins: Mixon RB $41k, Tagovailoa QB $29k, Matt Ryan QB $28k, Mostert RB $20k, Ridley WR $18k. League SF context: median win is just $4k, so his spikes move the market (RB p95 $39k, QB p95 $50k).
cards.vs_0008: Direct, repeated collision in Keith's core lanes. In 21 SF-era lots where both bid, Hammer won 11 and Keith won only 2 — and he overtook Keith (victim_fid=0008) six times: Mixon RB ($23k push), Godwin WR ($13k), Marquise Brown WR twice ($13k/$19k), Noah Fant TE ($3k), Diggs WR ($5k). His RB/QB-heavy spend overlaps Keith's positions almost exactly, so he's the owner most likely on the other side of your nominations. Handling: (1) He moves EARLY — don't out-wait him; by the time the clock's low he's usually already leading, so commit your real number up front. (2) Use his pounce reflex: nominate a tempting cap-free RB right after he just won one — he'll likely engage and burn cap/attention while your real target sits quiet. (3) On marquee RB/QB he tops out near $41k and rarely sustains marquee; go past ~$42k and you can break him, but expect him to push you the whole way (he matched Keith dollar-for-dollar on Mixon $41k and Mostert $20k before the tiebreak). (4) Don't get baited into bidding wars on mid-tier RBs — that's exactly where his 11-2 edge lives.
key_examples: 2023 Joe Mixon (RB) — Hammer's max win at $41k; he overtook Keith (0008) en route at $23k, then matched Keith dollar-for-dollar at $41k and won the tiebreak. Textbook 'wins the exact RB Keith wants.'
2023 Marquise Brown (WR) — Hammer overtook Keith TWICE (to $13k then $19k) and pushed the lot to $27k before losing to 0011 at $37k; a pure price-inflator who cost both Keith and the winner real cap.

2024 Noah Fant (TE) & 2025 Stefon Diggs (WR) — both lots he overtook Keith (0008) directly; on Fant he forced Keith up to the $4k winning bid, on Diggs he pushed Keith to a $14k commitment. He engages Keith specifically even on small lots.
2022 & 2024 Mostert / 2025 Geno Smith — three SF lots Hammer won outright over Keith (RB $11k, RB $20k, QB $15k), illustrating his 11-2 head-to-head dominance in the RB/QB lanes Keith plays.

cards.headline: A relentless cap-free grinder who lives at the bottom of the board and quietly muscles Keith on cheap-to-mid RBs.
cards.bid_rhythm: Bids in clustered, late-night/early-morning windows rather than spread across the day. SF-era peak_hours_et are [0, 10, 7] (midnight, 10am, 7am ET) — the hour histogram spikes at hour 0 (21 bids), hour 10 (21), hour 7 (19), and hour 9 (17), with a second cluster at hour 22-23 (11 + 16). He is a heavy late-clock presence: late_bid_share under8h=0.463 and under2h=0.407, meaning ~41% of his bids land with under 2 hours left on the 24h lock. He is not a daytime drip-bidder; expect his pressure in the overnight/pre-dawn ET window and in the final hours of a lot.
cards.snipe_threat: Genuine pouncer. SF-era post_win_pounce_share=0.511 (he bids on another lot within 8h after 51% of his wins), avg_followups=0.79. The chains are concrete: after winning Kareem Hunt ($22k, 2022-08-01 07:19) he immediately worked Matt Gay (PK), Foyesade Oluokun (LB) and D'Onta Foreman (RB) within the window; after Jordan Mason ($2k, 2022-08-07) he chased D'Ernest Johnson up to $4k. But note the followups are almost all cap-free/cheap dart-throws ($2-4k), not marquee swoops — he keeps the conveyor belt moving rather than escalating into a big lot.
cards.lurk_threat: High as an underbidder, low as a closer. SF-era runner_up_n=21 (28 over L5) — he is frequently the bridesmaid who pushes the winner up and loses. overtake_rate is only 0.19 with late_overtake_n=5, and lurk_win_n=0, so he forces prices but rarely steals lots late. Concrete pushes: David Montgomery 2025 (bid to $17k, lost to 0001 at $20k), Stefon Diggs 2025 (to $12k, lost to 0001 at $20k), Allen Robinson 2022 (to $12k, lost to 0009 at $21k), Myles Garrett 2023 (to $7k, lost to 0007 at $13k). He inflates lots more than he wins them.
cards.spend_signature: Deep-value specialist. SF-era zone_mix is 87.2% cap-free (2-4k), 8.5% low, 2.1% mid, 2.1% marquee — by far a bottom-of-the-board operator (vs league cap-free share 61.1%). 47 wins on only 132k total = ~2.8k/win, right around the league median win of 4k. Top positions by spend: RB 63k, LB 19k, WR 17k, QB 11k. marquee_wins=1, max_win_k=22 (Kareem Hunt 2022 — his lone real splurge). His one big historical splash was Robert Woods at $41k in 2021 (pre-SF). He almost never plays in the 18k+ marquee tier where Keith's stars live.
cards.vs_0008: The overlap is RBs at the low-to-mid tier, and it is real. Direct SF-era collisions: he beat Keith for Cooper Kupp 2025 ($9k vs Keith's $7k), beat Keith for Najee Harris 2025 ($13k vs $8k), and tied Keith on Austin Ekeler 2025 (both at $8k, Keith won) and Keaton Mitchell ($2k each, 0006 won). With RB his #1 spend (63k SF) and ~41% of bids in the final 2 hours, he is exactly the guy who nudges Keith's value-RB targets up a tick or two in the closing window — death by a thousand cuts, not a knockout. Handling: do NOT bid early against him on a cheap RB (you just teach him the price and invite a late push); set a firm walk-away and be willing to let him have the $2-4k dart-throws — his pounce conveyor wants volume, not your $13k. On a genuine mid-RB you want (the Najee/Kupp tier), bid to your max in one clean overnight-ET move to close before his under-2h window opens, since he overtakes late only 19% of the time and has zero lurk-wins. He is NOT a marquee threat — your 18k+ stars are safe from him.
key_examples: Najee Harris (RB, 2025): 0006 won at $13k, directly outbidding Keith/0008's $8k — RB-vs-Keith collision he won.
Cooper Kupp (WR, 2025): 0006 won at $9k over Keith's $7k; one of the rare WRs where he closed.
Kareem Hunt (RB, 2022): his SF-era max win at $22k (07:19 ET), immediately followed within 8h by dart-throws on Matt Gay, Oluokun and Foreman — textbook pounce.
David Montgomery (RB, 2025): bid up to $17k but lost to 0001 at $20k — classic runner_up, inflated the lot without winning it (runner_up_n=21).

cards.headline: A barbell bidder who floods cap-free lots, then ambushes one marquee name per year — and he overtakes Keith's leaders more than almost anyone.
cards.bid_rhythm: High-volume and spread, not focused: 164 bids for 56 wins in the SF era (n_bids 164 / n_wins 56). peak_hours_et = [7, 14, 15] — an early-morning 7 ET spike (20 bids in that bucket) plus an early/mid-afternoon work-hours cluster (17 bids at 14 ET, 13 at 15 ET); the L5 hist adds a 21 ET dinner-hour window. He is NOT a midnight closer — he is around in nearly every hour bucket, most dangerous mid-day and at 9pm ET.
cards.snipe_threat: High post-win momentum. post_win_pounce_share = 0.571 (SF) — after more than half his wins he bids on another lot within 8h, post_win_avg_followups = 1.0. Landing one player feeds straight into the next bid. Concrete: in 2024 his Tyreek Hill ($61k) and James Conner ($20k) wins sit inside a same-window cluster of 16 final bids — winning marquee did not slow his dollar-tier churn at all.
cards.lurk_threat: Active over-the-top pusher, not a passive lurker (lurk_win_n = 0). overtake_rate = 0.177 with runner_up_n = 11 (SF) — eleven times he was the bridesmaid who pumped the price and lost, so he reliably inflates final prices even on lots he doesn't win. Late presence is heavy: late_bid_share under8h = 0.468, under6h = 0.45, under2h = 0.394 — ~40% of his bids land with under 2h on the clock. late_overtake_n = 3 (SF), so most of his bumps come at the 24h-reset mark rather than the final minutes, but he WILL stab late.
cards.spend_signature: Classic barbell. zone_mix = 82.1% cap-free (2-4K), 8.9% low, only 1.8% mid, 7.1% marquee — he ignores the middle tier and swings big a handful of times. marquee_wins = 4, max_win_k = 66 (Brady 2022, the league QB-price ceiling per position_thresholds_sf QB max=66). Top positional dollars: QB 77k, WR 74k, RB 51k, TE 45k, plus a real IDP appetite (DE 29k, S 22k). His four SF marquee strikes: Brady $66k (QB), Tyreek Hill $61k (WR, vs league WR p95=30/max=61 — he set the WR ceiling), Kittle $29k (TE — the league TE max), Conner $20k (RB).
cards.vs_0008: Direct threat: 0007 overtakes 0008 more than chance. In the SF era he listed Keith (0008) as his victim_fid on multiple over-the-top bumps — Alvin Kamara 2024 ($23k overtake), Chauncey Gardner-Johnson 2023 ($2k), and Josh Reynolds 2024 ($3k) all show vic=0008. In head-to-head contested lots he has beaten Keith outright (Myles Garrett $13k DE 2023, Josh Reynolds $3k WR 2024, Colby Parkinson $4k TE 2024, Gardner-Johnson $4k S 2023). Keith won the small-ball duels (Matt Gay PK, Ty Chandler RB, Mike White QB, Derwin James $9k S). TACTICAL: (1) On Keith's QB/WR marquee targets, expect Josh to be the one who pushes the price — he set both the QB ceiling (Brady 66) and WR ceiling (Hill 61), so budget for a real fight or let HIM overpay and pivot. (2) Do not nominate a cap-free name Keith actually wants while Josh is online at 7 ET or 14-15 ET — that is exactly his volume window and his pounce share is 57%. (3) His mid-tier (10-17K) is a blind spot (1.8% of spend) — that 10-17K band is the safest zone to land Keith's value plays uncontested. (4) Because his late_overtake_n is only 3, his bumps cluster at the 24h reset, not the last 2h — Keith can re-take a lot in the final hour and Josh is less likely to answer.
key_examples: 2022: WON Tom Brady $66k (QB) — his max win and the league's all-time QB price ceiling (overtook 0009 to do it); shows he will spend top-of-market on a SuperFlex QB.
2024: WON Tyreek Hill $61k (WR), overtaking victim 0004 — set the league WR price ceiling (WR p95=30, max=61), proving one elite WR strike per year.
2024: OVERTOOK Keith (0008) on Alvin Kamara at $23k with 41.7h left, then 0002 ultimately won at $27k — textbook 0007: he bumps Keith's leader early and drives the price up even when he loses.

2023 & 2024 head-to-head wins over 0008: Myles Garrett $13k DE (2023) and Colby Parkinson $4k TE / Josh Reynolds $3k WR (2024, both with vic=0008) — he out-finishes Keith on mid/cheap lots they both want.

cards.headline: A patient cap-free grinder who almost never opens the wallet — but when he locks onto a marquee RB, he will chase it to the moon (Henry $94K) and won't blink at a 31-bid war.
cards.bid_rhythm: Bids cluster at three peak ET hours: 0 (midnight), 12 (noon) and 5am (peak_hours_et [0,12,5] SF; [0,5,12] l5) — a wraparound spread, not one window. The hour_hist confirms a true bimodal: 45 bids at hour 0 and a noon hump (33 at hr 12). He is highly late-active: 41.9% of his bids land with under 8h on the clock, 38.9% under 6h, and 31.9% under 2h to lock (SF) — virtually identical in l5 (40.3/37.4/31.3). Translation: a third of everything he does is a last-2-hour move, and he is just as likely to fire at 5am as at noon, so he is hard to time out by waiting for him to log off.
cards.snipe_threat: Moderate-to-high serial pouncer. post_win_pounce_share 0.547 (SF) / 0.522 (l5) — after more than half his wins he is bidding on another lot within 8h, averaging 1.49 follow-ups (SF) / 1.41 (l5). Concrete: 2022 after winning Mecole Hardman he bid on 3 other lots inside 8h; after Irv Smith Jr., Tyler Huntley, Jashaun Corbin, and (2023) Tress Way / Samaje Perine / Derwin James he chained onto 2 more lots each. He doesn't go quiet after a win — winning seems to free up cap he immediately redeploys onto the next cheap target.
cards.lurk_threat: This is his single most disruptive trait. runner_up_n is 48 (SF) / 59 (l5) — he is constantly the bridesmaid who pushes the winner up and walks away empty. lurk_win_n is 0 (he doesn't snipe-and-hold quietly), but overtake_rate is 0.18 with late_overtake_n 12 (SF), so ~1-in-5 of his bids flip the lead and a dozen of those came inside the final 8h. He drove up and LOST: Rodgers 2023 ($50K, to 0011), Mixon 2023 ($41K, to 0005), Cousins 2022 ($37K, to 0003), Derrick Henry 2024 ($34K, to 0003), Hopkins 2022 ($32K, to 0002). He is the guy sitting underneath your marquee bid forcing you to overpay — a tax engine more than a sniper.
cards.spend_signature: Extreme cap-free/value tilt: zone_mix is 88% cap-free (2-4K), 6.7% low, 2.7% mid, only 2.7% marquee in SF — far below the league mix (cap-free 61.1%, marquee 12.6%). Median win is the league-floor 4K. Spend is overwhelmingly RB-first: pos_spend RB $171K, then WR $53K, S $19K, TE $17K, QB $13K (SF). He punts QB in SF (only $13K, just a $5K Garoppolo and $4K-tier dart) — a real soft spot in a superflex format. marquee_wins is just 2 (SF) / 4 (l5), and his max_win is $94K — the 2023 Derrick Henry, a 31-bid slugfest where he traded forced bids with 0004 and 0010 from $25K all the way to the top. Other big swings: Hubbard $37K (2025), and historically Damien Williams $50K (2019), Lamar Miller $46K (2015). When he commits to a lead RB he is essentially unbeatable on price.
cards.vs_0008: Since this card IS Keith, read it as self-scouting / how rivals exploit him. (1) His QB spend is the hole — $13K total in SF means superflex QB is where rivals expect him to fold; if Keith wants to stop being out-positioned he must budget a real QB swing, not punt. (2) He bleeds value as a perennial runner-up (48 bridesmaid losses): rivals already know that if Keith is on a marquee RB they can let him force the price and snipe a different one, OR bait him into a war and bail (0004 did exactly this on Henry 2023, riding him to $94K). Keith should set a hard walk number per marquee lot and stop reflexively re-forcing. (3) His tells are loud: cap-free 88% mix + 5am/noon/midnight peaks + 32% under-2h bids mean opponents can predict both WHAT (cheap RB depth) and WHEN (overnight + final 2h) he'll strike, and pre-empt his cap-free targets with an early 5K. To threaten the field rather than be taxed by it, Keith should diversify off the RB/cap-free script and disguise his late-window timing.
key_examples: 2023 Derrick Henry (RB, $94K, max_win): Keith's signature win — a 31-bid war he opened at $25K and dragged through forced exchanges with 0004 and 0010 to $94K, the largest RB price in the l5 board. Proof he will not lose a lead RB he wants, at any cost.

2023 Aaron Rodgers (QB) — Keith was the runner-up who forced it to $50K and LOST to 0011; mirrored by Mixon 2023 ($41K to 0005) and Cousins 2022 ($37K to 0003). Three of his ~48 bridesmaid losses, the core of his price-tax pattern.

2022 post-win pounce: after winning Mecole Hardman he bid on 3 separate other lots within 8h (and 2 more each after Irv Smith Jr., Huntley, Corbin) — concrete evidence of the 54.7% pounce share and 1.49 follow-ups.

Zone signature: 88% of SF-era wins are cap-free 2-4K (median win 4K) with RB the dominant position ($171K of $299K), vs a league that runs 12.6% marquee — Keith is a volume value-grinder, not a marquee buyer, with QB ($13K) the conspicuous gap in a superflex era.

cards.headline: Dawn-patrol RB hoarder who bumps you early and lurks as a chronic bridesmaid — loud volume, but never a final-window sniper.
cards.bid_rhythm: Pure dawn-patrol, focused not spread. SF peak_hours_et are [6,7,5] and the hour_hist is brutally front-loaded: 22 bids at 5 ET, 54 at 6 ET, 42 at 7 ET — that's 118 of 234 SF bids (about half) fired before 8am ET, with a smaller midday cluster at 11-13 ET (17/16/12) and a thin evening dribble at 19-20 ET (7/12). His late_bid_share is only moderate (under8h 0.406, under6h 0.376, under2h 0.339), so he is NOT camping the 24h lock — his pressure is a concentrated early-morning window, not a final-minutes vigil.
cards.snipe_threat: Moderate, not a rampager. post_win_pounce_share is 0.431 with post_win_avg_followups of 1.37 — after roughly 4 of every 10 of his 65 SF wins he flips to another lot within 8h, but only one or two follow-ups, not a feeding frenzy. He grabs a value piece and keeps shopping the dollar bin the same morning rather than chain-sniping a whole tier. Manageable: winning a lot won't trigger him to strip three more off you in the next 8 hours.
cards.lurk_threat: This is his signature and the real annoyance. runner_up_n=31 in the SF era — a chronic underbidder/bridesmaid who pushes winners up and loses. The CSV shows 58 SF lots he bid on and lost, including pushing Brady to $66k (lost to 0007), Tua to $29k (lost 0005), and Henry to $23k (lost 0003). BUT the timing defuses the swoop threat: late_overtake_n=2 and all 34 of his SF overtakes land at t_to_close >= 24h (median 26.2h, minimum 24.0h) — ZERO inside the 8h close window. He bumps the leader early to set a price, then sits. He inflates what you pay; he almost never steals at the buzzer.
cards.spend_signature: Dollar-store specialist with one RB splurge gear. zone_mix is 0.877 capfree (2-4K), just 0.015 low / 0.046 mid / 0.062 marquee — he lives in the cheap pool and rarely touches the top end (only 4 marquee_wins). But when he does climb, it's for a back: pos_spend_k is RB $139k (far and away #1), QB $43k, WR $29k, with IDP sprinkles (DE $15k, LB $14k, S $11k). RB is 22.6% of his SF bids and QB 17.9%. His max_win_k is 57.0 — Ekeler in 2022 (won outright at seq 10). Other notable wins: Fournette $39k, Allen Robinson $21k, Mixon $19k, Pollard $17k. Total SF spend $259k across 65 wins (median win ~$2-4k, in line with league median_win_k_sf of 4).
cards.vs_0008: Bear is a price-inflater on Keith's exact turf, not a closer who beats him. His top spend is RB ($139k SF) and Keith's marquee target is RB (Keith won Derrick Henry for the league-high $94k in 2023, the top_wins_l5 leader) — so on any premium back Bear nominates or chases early, expect him to bump the price 24h+ out. His direct history with 0008 is thin and all early: only 3 SF bids ever victimized Keith — Fournette $31k (2022, overtake at 61.75h to close), and dollar bumps on Drake and Gus Edwards ($2k each, 2023) — and he has NEVER beaten Keith for a lot (0 of his 58 lost lots went to 0008). Handling: do NOT panic-bid in his 5-7am ET dawn window — that's when he sets inflated anchors he can't defend. Because he has zero late overtakes (all >=24h to close), Keith should hold fire on contested RBs and place the decisive bid inside the final 8h, where Bear simply isn't active. Let Bear be the bridesmaid (he's been one 31 times); slot in late at your true number and he won't re-engage. Only real caution: his moderate pounce (0.431) means after he wins a cheap RB he may dip into the value bin Keith also shops, so lock your $1-4k depth pieces before mid-morning rather than leaving them dangling.
key_examples: 2022 — Won Austin Ekeler (RB) for $57k, his max_win and a marquee splurge that fits his RB-first signature (won outright at seq 10).
2022 — Pushed Tom Brady (QB) all the way to $66k as the underbidder before losing to 0007; classic runner-up behavior (he was the runner_up_fid on that league-record QB lot).

2022 — His only meaningful shot at Keith: overtook 0008 on Leonard Fournette up to $31k, but did it 61.75h before close (early anchor, not a snipe) and still didn't win the player at his final number.
2023 — Dollar-bin bumps victimizing 0008 on Kenyan Drake and Gus Edwards ($2k each, ~24h to close), illustrating he tangles with Keith only in the cheap RB pool and only early in the cycle.

cards.headline: Cap-free volume grinder who turns into Keith's worst nightmare on marquee RBs — the underbidder who personally drove Henry to $94k.
cards.bid_rhythm: Heavy early-morning bidder with a focused triple-window, not a 24/7 sprayer. SF-era peak ET hours are 6, 12, 7 — hour 6 ET alone holds 70 of 321 bids (21.8%), hour 12 has 44 (13.7%), hour 7 has 42 (13.1%). So nearly half his activity lands in a dawn (6-7am ET) burst plus a midday lunch check. He also shows a small midnight cluster (hour 0 = 30 bids). Expect him to wake up and re-bid the overnight board before most owners are online.
cards.snipe_threat: Strong post-win pouncer. SF-era post_win_pounce_share is 0.578 with post_win_avg_followups of 2.27 — after 57.8% of his wins he bids on another lot within 8h, averaging 2.3 follow-up bids. He doesn't bank a win and sit; closing one lot is a trigger to keep hammering the board. The dawn-burst rhythm amplifies this: a 6am win rolls straight into more 6-7am bids on other lots.
cards.lurk_threat: This is his defining threat. SF-era runner_up_n is 53 — 53 times he was the underbidder/bridesmaid who pushed the winner up but LOST (62 in L5). Late-bid share is moderate (under8h 0.31, under6h 0.291, under2h 0.229), meaning ~23% of bids come inside the final 2h — he stays engaged to the lock but rarely lands the kill shot on a contested star.
cards.spend_signature: Extreme cap-free skew: 85.9% of SF-era bids are in the 2-4K cap-free zone, only 1.6% low, 4.7% mid, 7.8% marquee — well above the league's own marquee rate but on a tiny base. 64 wins / $286k total SF era; max win just $38k (twice). Position spend (SF): RB $86k, WR $82k, QB $53k lead, with real IDP volume — S $21k (11 wins), DE $15k (7), LB $13k (9). Win counts: 10 WR, 9 RB, 11 S, 9 LB, 7 DE, 5 QB. His 5 marquee wins are James Conner $38k + Mike Evans $38k (2022), then Brock Purdy $28k, D'Andre Swift $23k, Terry McLaurin $19k (2025). He buys real volume cheap and splashes occasionally on a mid-tier RB/WR/QB — he does NOT win the true blue-chips.
cards.vs_0008: Blake is the guy who makes Keith overpay. The 2023 Derrick Henry war is the case study: it ran 31 bids, and Blake (0010) was the runner_up_fid on Keith's eventual $94k win. Blake personally overtook Keith at $41k, $45k, $66k, $67k, $72k, $82k, and $87k — Keith only closed at $94k because Blake forced him from a ~$50k zone up another $44k. Blake's victim_fid=0008 list is stacked: he bumped Keith on Henry ($82k, $87k), Marquise Brown ($24k WR), David Montgomery ($12k RB), Myles Garrett ($9k DE). Tactically: (1) If Keith wants a marquee RB/WR — Blake's top spend positions — assume Blake will sit underneath and tax every increment; don't slow-play, jump to a credible number early to break his will rather than trading $1-4k bumps for hours. (2) Blake's overtake_rate is only 0.215 and late_overtake_n=13 — he rarely actually closes from behind, so on a lot Keith truly wants, holding the lead into the final 2h is usually safe; the danger is the price, not the loss. (3) Exploit the dawn window: Blake re-bids at 6-7am ET, so a Keith bid placed AFTER his morning burst (late morning/midday) gives Blake fewer cheap re-touch cycles before the lock. (4) On Keith's cap-free IDP/depth targets (S/LB/DE), expect Blake there in volume — let him have the $2-4k throwaways and save ammo, because that's where 85.9% of his bids and most of his wins live.
key_examples: 2023 Derrick Henry (RB): 31-bid war, Blake (0010) the runner-up who drove Keith (0008) from a ~$50k position to a $94k winning close — Blake overtook Keith at $82k (seq 26) and $87k (seq 28) before Keith finally shut it at $94k.

2023 Aaron Rodgers (QB): Blake led the lot at $36k (08:20 ET) before 0011 swooped to $50k — Blake the runner-up, classic price-pusher who loses the star (his QB max is modest; the win went elsewhere).

2022 marquee splashes: Blake's two biggest wins ever, James Conner $38k (RB, won 12pm ET) and Mike Evans $38k (WR, won 7am ET in his dawn window) — both mid-tier, both his ceiling; he has never won a true blue-chip.
2025 mid-tier buys: Brock Purdy $28k QB, D'Andre Swift $23k RB, Terry McLaurin $19k WR — all closed at 12-14 ET, confirming his midday-finish habit on the few lots he actually lands.

cards.headline: QB-obsessed price-inflator who lurks as the underbidder on marquee QBs/WRs and pounces on a second lot right after winning.
cards.bid_rhythm: Bimodal and predictable. SF-era hour histogram peaks at 5am ET (26 bids), then a second wall at noon-1pm ET (12h=24, 13h=22) — peak_hours_et [5,12,13]. He is an early-morning sniper and a lunch-hour grinder, not an evening bidder (17h-23h are sparse, mostly 3-8 bids). He is NOT a focused last-minute closer: late_bid_share is heavy and spread (under8h 0.481, under6h 0.427, under2h 0.382) — nearly half his bids come in with under 8h left, but they're scattered across many lots rather than concentrated sniping on one. Expect him to surface in the morning window and again midday across multiple lots simultaneously.
cards.snipe_threat: Real and above-median. post_win_pounce_share 0.569 — after 57% of his SF wins he bids on ANOTHER lot within 8h (post_win_avg_followups 1.26). Winning one player does NOT take him off the board; it tends to free up his attention/cap for the next target. If Keith and 0011 are contesting parallel lots, expect 0011 to keep applying pressure on the second lot immediately after closing the first.
cards.lurk_threat: This is his signature threat. runner_up_n 12 in the SF era — twelve times he was the bridesmaid who pushed the winner up and lost, repeatedly at the top of the market: he forced Ekeler to $57k (lost to 0009 at the same $57k), Carr to $38k (lost to 0001), Cousins to $37k (lost to 0003), Tyreek Hill to a $35k push (Hill closed at $61k to 0007, with 0011 the listed runner-up), McCaffrey to $32k (lost to 0004 at $56k), and Dak to $36k (lost to 0004 at $45k). overtake_rate 0.169 with late_overtake_n 5 — he does swoop late (Marquise Brown overtaken at $32k with 3.57h left, Donald/Minshew with ~6-7h left), but more often he is the relentless underbidder who detonates the price ceiling and walks away empty. He is the man who makes you overpay, even when he doesn't win.
cards.spend_signature: Cap-free heavy on volume, QB-funded at the top. zone_mix is 70.7% capfree (2-4K), 13.8% low, 10.3% mid, only 5.2% marquee — but marquee_wins 3 and max_win_k 51.0 (Justin Herbert, 2025, won at seq6 in the noon ET window, t_remaining 0.0h). Position spend is overwhelmingly QB ($132k, 40% of his $327k SF total) then WR ($99k, 30%) — QB+WR = 71% of everything. Notable SF wins: Herbert $51k, Aaron Rodgers $50k (2023), Marquise Brown $37k, Carson Wentz $17k, Stefon Diggs $16k, Roquan Smith LB $15k. He chases startable QBs aggressively and a steady stream of cap-free WR/IDP dart throws.
cards.vs_0008: Limited direct collision but a genuine price-inflation tax on Keith's WR buys. Keith (0008) is RB-funded ($171k/57% on RB, max $94k Henry) and barely touches QB ($13k); 0011 is the inverse (71% QB+WR). They do NOT fight over RBs, so Keith's marquee-RB lane is largely clear of 0011. The overlap is WR: 0011 spent $99k there and is a chronic marquee-WR underbidder. Tactic: (1) On WRs Keith truly wants, expect 0011 to bid him up to his max even though 0011 usually loses — pad your ceiling or be ready to let a lot go that 0011 has over-juiced. (2) Use 0011 as a stalking horse: if Keith does NOT want a QB, let 0011 spend his big QB cap (Herbert $51k, Rodgers $50k) elsewhere — every dollar he sinks into QBs is cap he can't bring to Keith's WR/RB targets. (3) Time discipline: he hits the 5am ET and noon-1pm ET windows and bids with <8h left on many lots at once; do not assume an early-quiet lot is safe — recheck after his midday wave. (4) After 0011 wins a lot, treat the next 8h as elevated-pressure on adjacent lots (57% pounce rate), so don't open your own nomination right behind his win.
key_examples: 2025 Justin Herbert (QB): won at $51k (his max_win_k), seq6 in the noon-ET window with t_remaining 0.0h — his top marquee strike of the SF era.
2022 JuJu Smith-Schuster (WR): direct H2H — Keith (0008) won at $15k and 0011 pushed the price to exactly $15k over 2 bids, forcing Keith to the ceiling.
2022 Austin Ekeler (RB): 0011 the bridesmaid, pushed to $57k over 3 bids and still lost to 0009 at $57k — textbook underbidder who detonates the market (one of his runner_up_n=12).
2024 Tyreek Hill (WR) / 2025 Christian McCaffrey (RB): listed runner-up on both marquee lots (Hill closed $61k to 0007, CMC $56k to 0004), pushing each toward its ceiling before bowing out.

cards.headline: High-volume late-night WR scrounger who lives in the cap-free pool but will spike to $24K when a target gets personal — and he's beaten Keith head-to-head three times.

He works a WIDE front, not a focused one — 152 bids for only 43 wins (SF), blanketing 6-8 lots in a single 10pm-11pm window (e.g. 2024-07-29 he had live bids on Evans, Brown, Lockett, Ertz and Warner all between 20:33 and 22:42 ET).
cards.snipe_threat: Moderate-but-real. post_win_pounce_share 0.442 — after nearly half his wins he's bidding another lot within 8h, though post_win_avg_followups is only 1.02, so it's one fresh poke, not a flurry. He doesn't disengage after a win; expect him to redeploy leftover cap onto the next cheap WR/TE on the board.
cards.lurk_threat: This is his real edge. runner_up_n 18 (SF) — he is constantly the bridesmaid who jacks up the winner's price. overtake_rate 0.283 but late_overtake_n only 3 and lurk_win_n 0, so he rarely steals at the buzzer; instead he sits as the underbidder and inflates. He pushed Davante Adams to $30K (lost to 0004), Godwin to $27K, Travis Kelce to $21K (two separate pushes), and forced Keith's own Garoppolo to $5K in 2022. A price-driver, not a closer — dangerous as a cost-inflator on anything Keith actually wants.
cards.spend_signature: Bargain-bin volume buyer. zone_mix is 74.4% cap-free ($2-4K), 20.9% low, just 2.3% mid and 2.3% marquee — total_k 155 across 43 wins (median win sits at the league's $4K floor). Heavily WR-tilted: pos_spend WR 66 / TE 28 / RB 18 / QB 16 (LB 10, DE 7). Only ONE marquee_win and his max_win_k is 24.0 (Mike Evans 2024) — well under the SF WR p95 of $30K and a fraction of the league's $94K ceiling. He floods the cheap WR/TE shelf and only once in four years climbed into the $20K+ tier.
cards.vs_0008: Two distinct threats. (1) Direct WR competition: his #1 spend is WR ($66K SF) and Keith's WR is his #2 spend ($53K SF), so they collide in the mid-WR pool — and Klingenberg has already WON three head-to-head lots off Keith (Tannehill $16K QB 2022, Michael Thomas $6K WR 2023, Keenan Allen $5K WR 2025, all with 0008 forcing). (2) Cost-inflation: with runner_up_n 18 he's the league's premier price-pumper and forced Keith's Garoppolo to $5K. Counter-play: Keith's bread-and-butter is RB ($171K SF spend) where Klingenberg barely plays (RB only $18K, max single win $24K) — Keith's marquee RB targets are safe from him, so let him have the cheap WR shelf. Where they overlap on a mid-WR/TE, exploit his deadline habit: he posts ~38% of bids inside the final 2h and peaks at hour 23, so a clean over-the-top bid placed AFTER his 11pm ET push leaves him little room to re-raise before lock. Do NOT get baited into a $20K+ WR war late at night — that's the exact 22:00-22:42 window where he drove Evans from $8K to $24K.
